# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

/**
 * Validation liveness (gh-821) — the arm-must-mean-a-live-run state machine.
 *
 * Live fa PR #1443 (2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z): the dispatched validation run
 * concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family) while the
 * `ai_validating` arm stayed on; the stale-arm sweeper skipped it ("no
 * concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") and four
 * validated PRs deferred on the mutex for ~2h until a manual
 * `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. CANCELLED is never a
 * VERDICT (gh-755 — no rework on a cancel), but a cancel (or a lost
 * dispatch) behind an arm is a ZOMBIE: the mutex is held with no live run
 * behind it, which is exactly what the serial slot must never do.
 *
 * This module is the pure half of the fix:
 *
 *   classify(probe)  — the liveness state machine over a
 *                      probeDispatchedState bundle: 'running' (in-flight,
 *                      or concluded inside the check-visibility grace),
 *                      'green' / 'red' (verdict paths — callers keep their
 *                      existing consumption), 'zombie-cancelled' /
 *                      'zombie-no-run' (the arm holds the slot with no
 *                      live run; caller re-dispatches, bounded).
 *   zombie marks     — durable per-head re-dispatch bookkeeping carried in
 *                      marker comments (the red-head/empty-lap carrier:
 *                      per-PR state with zero extra infrastructure). One
 *                      marker per re-dispatch gives the crash-loop guard
 *                      (3 in a row on the same head ⇒ park) and the rate

## Description

**Evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, ticks 13:5x–15:2xZ 2026-10-16):** PR #1615 carries `priority_blocker` but its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` no longer exists (fork branch deleted). Every tick: ``\🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot`` → ``\⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json`` → the slot dies with it. Queue frozen for hours; operator hand-removed the label and was correctly overruled (PR-as-carrier rule: work items must keep moving).

**Ask (fail-open dispatch):**
1. A candidate whose trigger fails (422 no-ref, or any non-retryable dispatch error) must NOT consume the dispatch slot: skip it with a recorded reason and continue down the FIFO — the slot goes to the next candidate in the same tick.
2. The preemption rule inherits the same fail-open: a priority blocker that cannot be dispatched yields the slot instead of holding it (it keeps the label; it just can't hold a slot it can't use).
3. After N consecutive trigger failures on one head (suggest 3), park the PR with `validation_failed` + a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch — parked items don't preempt (consistent with the existing sticky-park rule).

Keep the PR-as-carrier contract: legs anchor to PR or issue interchangeably (live dart 2026-10-16: gh-382/gh-384 rework legs ran PR-only, no issue). The fix restores movement without dropping any label semantics.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

This is the dmtools-agents repo. The ticket is gh-922: "SM: a candidate whose workflow trigger 422s (missing head ref) consumes the slot and starves the whole FIFO queue".

The SM agent is `sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`. The bug is about dispatch logic in the SM agent: when a candidate PR's workflow trigger fails (422 no-ref), the dispatch slot is consumed and the FIFO queue is starved.

Ask:
1. A candidate whose trigger fails (422 no-ref, or any non-retryable dispatch error) must NOT consume the dispatch slot: skip it with a recorded reason and continue down the FIFO — the slot goes to the next candidate in the same tick.
2. The preemption rule inherits the same fail-open: a priority blocker that cannot be dispatched yields the slot instead of holding it.
3. After N consecutive trigger failures one head (suggest 3), park the PR with `validation_failed` + a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch — parked items don't preempt.

Now I understand the flow:

1. `sourceMod.query(rule, ...)` returns tickets — for githubSource, `matched.slice(0, limit)`.
2. The loop iterates `tickets`, dispatches each until `effectiveLimit` processed or budget exhausted.
3. When `triggerWorkflow` fails (422), `triggered=false`, the key is not added to processedKeys, budget not decremented, loop continues to the next ticket... BUT with `limit: 1`, tickets contains only ONE candidate. So the loop ends without dispatching anything. The next tick queries again and gets the same one candidate (the blocker with dead head). Queue frozen.

So the root cause is at TWO levels:
- githubSource.query's `matched.slice(0, limit)` discards the non-blocker candidates before the trigger is even attempted; a failed dispatch cannot fall through to candidates that were cut by the limit.
- triggerWorkflow's catch swallows ALL errors the same way (returns false), and there's no "recorded reason" or consecutive-failure tracking, so the same dead-head PR is re-selected every tick.

The ask:
1. A candidate whose trigger fails (422 no-ref, or any non-retryable dispatch error) must NOT consume the dispatch slot: skip with recorded reason and continue down the FIFO — the slot goes to the next candidate in the same tick.
2. Priority blocker preemption inherits fail-open: a blocker that cannot be dispatched yields the slot (keeps label).
3. After N consecutive trigger failures one head (suggest 3), park the PR with `validation_failed` + comment telling the author to restore/re-push — parked items don't preempt.

Now, how to implement? Options:

**Option A**: Make the query return MORE than limit candidates (e.g. limit + N extra), and let the dispatch loop fall through to the extras when a trigger fails.

**Option B**: Make triggerWorkflow detect non-retryable failures (422 "No ref found", 404 etc.), and on such failure: record reason, track consecutive failures per head, and if within the same rule's remaining candidate list there are more candidates, continue. But `tickets` is already sliced to `limit` at query time.

The cleanest minimal fix respecting the architecture:

# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). ## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). ## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). 3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

- The dispatch loop's candidate list for a rule is already sliced at query time (`githubSource.queryPrs` → `matched.slice(0, limit)`). For a limit-1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated), the tier-aware sort puts the priority_blocker first; the 6 non-blockers are CUT before any dispatch is attempted. When the blocker's trigger 422s, `triggered=false` → not in processedKeys, budget NOT decremented — but there are NO more candidates in `tickets` to fall through to. Next tick: same query, same dead-head blocker, same 422. Queue frozen.
- No consecutive-failure tracking → the dead head is retried forever, never parked.

**Fix approach (matching the ask):**

1. **Overfetch candidates at query time** so the loop can fall through when a trigger fails. In `githubSource.queryPrs`: keep `limit` + a small reserve (e.g. `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE`) — but ONLY items beyond `limit` are marked as fallthrough-only (they must not be dispatched unless an earlier candidate's trigger failed). Hmm — how does the loop know?

That's consistent with "skipped items don't consume slots" — actually wait, that CHANGES behavior for skip-labels: today, a limit:1 rule whose first candidate carries a skip label dispatches the second candidate (since skipped don't push processedKeys). So fallthrough-on-skip ALREADY happens today within the limit-sliced list. Overfetching extends the same semantics to trigger failures. Good — consistent.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

/**
 * Validation liveness (gh-821) — the arm-must-mean-a-live-run state machine.
 *
 * Live fa PR #1443 (2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z): the dispatched validation run
 * concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family) while the
 * `ai_validating` arm stayed on; the stale-arm sweeper skipped it ("no
 * concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") and four
 * validated PRs deferred on the mutex for ~2h until a manual
 * `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. CANCELLED is never a
 * VERDICT (gh-755 — no rework on a cancel), but a cancel (or a lost
 * dispatch) behind an arm is a ZOMBIE: the mutex is held with no live run
 * behind it, which is exactly what the serial slot must never do.
 *
 * This module is the pure half of the fix:
 *
 *   classify(probe)  — the liveness state machine over a
 *                      probeDispatchedState bundle: 'running' (in-flight,
 *                      or concluded inside the check-visibility grace),
 *                      'green' / 'red' (verdict paths — callers keep their
 *                      existing consumption), 'zombie-cancelled' /
 *                      'zombie-no-run' (the arm holds the slot with no
 *                      live run; caller re-dispatches, bounded).
 *   zombie marks     — durable per-head re-dispatch bookkeeping carried in
 *                      marker comments (the red-head/empty-lap carrier:
 *                      per-PR state with zero extra infrastructure). One
 *                      marker per re-dispatch gives the crash-loop guard
 *                      (3 in a row on the same head ⇒ park) and the rate
 *                      bound (1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour).
 *
 * Probe-error degeneracy: newestDispatchedRun fails CLOSED (null on error
 * AND on an empty list), so a degraded read classifies as 'zombie-no-run'.
 * That is the documented fail-open contract of the dispatch guards — the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). 3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`).
