{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). 3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable error (422 "No ref found" — the head branch was deleted on the fork) consumes the SM dispatch slot every tick, so the whole FIFO queue behind it starves.

**Root cause**: two cooperating defects:

1. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` — the candidate list is sliced to `matched.slice(0, limit)` (line ~809) at QUERY time, before any dispatch is attempted. For a limit:1 rule (validate-armed / merge-validated) the tier-aware sort puts the `priority_blocker` PR first and CUTS every non-blocker from the returned array. When the blocker's trigger then 422s, the SM engine loop (`js/smAgent.js` `processRule`) has zero remaining candidates to fall through to — `triggered=false` pushes nothing to `processedKeys`, the loop ends, the tick dispatches nothing.
2. `js/smAgent.js` `triggerWorkflow()` catch (line ~616) — ANY dispatch error is swallowed the same way: one `console.warn`, `return false`. The failure is not classified (no-ref vs transient), no reason is recorded on the PR, and there is no consecutive-failure counter — so the same dead-head candidate is re-selected and re-fails every tick, forever. Nothing ever parks it.

Live evidence (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, 2026-10-16): PR #1615 carried `priority_blocker`, its head ref `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` was deleted on the fork; every tick logged `🥇 priority blocker pr-1615 preempts the FIFO queue — 6 non-blocker PR(s) yield the slot` → `⚠️ Workflow trigger failed for pr-1615 (422): No ref found for: fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → the slot died with it for hours.

**Impact**: any limit-capped PR rule whose head candidate cannot be dispatched (deleted fork branch, renamed ref) freezes its whole lane — validation arms, merges, review legs — for as long as the dead head stays ahead of the FIFO. The preemption rule amplifies it: a dead-head blocker holds the slot against all non-blockers indefinitely.

**Fix approach** (fail-open dispatch, three parts):

1. **Fallthrough candidates at the source** — `queryPrs()` over-fetches: returns `limit + TRIGGER_FALLTHROUGH_RESERVE` (3) tier-sorted candidates instead of `limit`. The SM loop already gives skipped/failed candidates no slot credit (`processedKeys` only grows on success), so when a trigger fails the loop walks to the next candidate in the SAME tick; when nothing fails, `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit` breaks at exactly `limit` successes — today's limit semantics are preserved. A priority blocker that cannot be dispatched therefore yields the slot to the next candidate automatically (it keeps its label — PR-as-carrier untouched).
2. **Recorded reason + head-failure parking** — the `triggerWorkflow()` catch classifies the error (new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`). Non-retryable no-ref-class failures (422 / "No ref found") on a PR-carrier item post a durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <sha> — attempt N/cap` marker comment on the PR (same marker-comment bookkeeping pattern as the gh-821 zombie markers). After `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap` (default 3) consecutive failures on the SAME head, the PR is parked `validation_failed` with a comment telling the author to restore/re-push the branch; the park comment carries `parked-head: <sha>` so the existing #633/gh-750 sticky-park RESET ladder clears it when the branch is back (human push, new head).
3. **Parked items don't preempt** — in the `queryPrs()` tier sort, a `validation_failed`-labeled item has its `blocker` tier voided to `medium`, so a parked PR can never jump the FIFO (it also stops logging 🥇 preemption lines); consistent with the existing sticky-park rule where parked PRs leave the merge-window lanes entirely.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this issue.
"}

```markdown
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) + `test_smGithubSource.js` (3)
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed; `run_smAgent` 540/540; `run_smGithubSource` 70/70
- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) + `test_smGithubSource.js` (3)
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed; `run_smAgent` 540/540; `run_smGithubSource` 70/70
- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) + `test_smGithubSource.js` (3)
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed; `run_smAgent` 540/540; `run_smGithubSource` 70/70
- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) + `test_smGithubSource.js` (3)

- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

{"content":"### Root Cause
- A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` at query time, so a limit:1 rule returned ONLY the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours, re-failing every tick).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates. The engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick — an undispatchable priority blocker yields the slot and keeps its label (PR-as-carrier untouched). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium: parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js` + new `js/common/triggerFailures.js`: the trigger catch classifies the error. No-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures on one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment — `parked-head: <sha>` keys the existing #633 sticky-park RESET probes, so a re-push clears the park automatically. Transient failures fall through log-only. The `validate_pr` CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9 tests), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) and `test_smGithubSource.js` (3); registered in `run_all.json` / `run_triggerFailures.json`.
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed. `run_smAgent` 540/540, `run_smGithubSource` 70/70.
- `run_agentValidator`'s 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified via worktree).

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking; the fail-open slot yield is independent of it.
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests pinned the old exact `limit:1` slice; re-asserted as head-first pacing + fallthrough reserve (dispatch pacing stays engine-side, unchanged).

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

{"content":"### Root Cause
- A PR candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` at query time, so a limit:1 rule returned ONLY the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours, re-failing every tick).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates. The engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick — an undispatchable priority blocker yields the slot and keeps its label (PR-as-carrier untouched). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium: parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js` + new `js/common/triggerFailures.js`: the trigger catch classifies the error. No-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures on one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment — `parked-head: <sha>` keys the existing #633 sticky-park RESET probes, so a re-push clears the park automatically. Transient failures fall through log-only. The `validate_pr` CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9 tests), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) and `test_smGithubSource.js` (3); registered in `run_all.json` / `run_triggerFailures.json`.
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed. `run_smAgent` 540/540, `run_smGithubSource` 70/70.
- `run_agentValidator`'s 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified via worktree).

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking; the fail-open slot yield is independent of it.
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests pinned the old exact `limit:1` slice; re-asserted as head-first pacing + fallthrough reserve (dispatch pacing stays engine-side, unchanged).

```markdown
### Root Cause
A candidate whose workflow dispatch fails with a non-retryable 422 ("No ref found" — head branch deleted on the fork) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick. `queryPrs` sliced the candidate list to `limit` BEFORE dispatch, so a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head; the failed trigger left `processedKeys` empty with nothing left to try — the FIFO starved (live: a `priority_blocker` PR preempted 6 non-blockers for hours).

### Fix
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: `queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate in the SAME tick (blockers included: an undispatchable blocker yields the slot, keeps its label). A `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided to medium — parked items never preempt.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `triggerWorkflow`'s catch classifies the error (`js/common/triggerFailures.js`): no-ref failures post a `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` marker on the PR; after 3 consecutive failures one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment (`parked-head:` sha keys the existing #633 RESET probes — a re-push clears the park). Transient failures fall through log-only. The validate_pr CI-dispatch path gets the same fail-open continue.
- PR-as-carrier untouched: no label semantics change; legs still anchor to PR or issue.

### Test Coverage
- New: `test_triggerFailures.js` (9), gh-922 suites in `test_smAgent.js` (7) + `test_smGithubSource.js` (3)
- `run_all.json`: 2940 passed, 0 failed; `run_smAgent` 540/540; `run_smGithubSource` 70/70
- `run_agentValidator` 28 failures are pre-existing on the base commit (verified)

### Notes
- `jobParams.triggerFailParkCap=false` disables markers/parking (fail-open yield stays).
- Two gh-759/gh-829 tests re-asserted the old exact `limit:1` slice; updated to head-first + fallthrough-reserve (dispatch pacing is engine-side, unchanged).
```

All verification passed. Final state: working tree clean, all changes committed to `ai/gh-922`.

## Summary

**Bug gh-922**: a PR whose head ref was deleted (422 "No ref found" on dispatch) consumed the SM dispatch slot every tick and starved the whole FIFO queue — a `priority_blocker` dead head preempted 6 non-blockers for hours.

**Root cause**: `queryPrs` sliced candidates to `limit` at query time (a limit:1 rule returned only the dead head), and `triggerWorkflow`'s catch swallowed every error identically — no classification, no record, no park, so the dead head was re-selected forever.

**Fix (fail-open dispatch, all three asks)**:
1. `githubSource.queryPrs` over-fetches `limit + 3` tier-sorted candidates — the engine loop already gives failed candidates no slot credit, so a failed trigger falls through to the next candidate **in the same tick**; a `validation_failed`-parked item's blocker tier is voided (parked items never preempt).
2. The trigger catch (AI-leg + `validate_pr` CI-dispatch paths) classifies errors via new pure module `js/common/triggerFailures.js`; no-ref failures post durable `⚠️ trigger-failed <branch> — attempt N/3` markers on the PR.
3. After 3 consecutive failures on one head (`jobParams.triggerFailParkCap`, tunable/disableable) the PR parks `validation_failed` with a restore/re-push comment; `parked-head: <sha>` keys the existing #633 sticky-park RESET probes, so a re-push clears it automatically. PR-as-carrier and all label semantics untouched.

**Tests**: TDD — 6 reproduction tests confirmed failing first, then green. `run_all.json` 2940/2940, `run_smAgent` 540/540, `run_smGithubSource` 70/70, new `test_triggerFailures` 9/9. The 28 `run_agentValidator` failures verified pre-existing on the base commit via worktree.
